<h1 id="unleash-api">Unleash API v8.3.1</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://eu.app.unleash-hosted.com/demo">https://eu.app.unleash-hosted.com/demo</a>

# Authentication

* API Key (apiKey)
    - Parameter Name: **Authorization**, in: header. API key needed to access this API

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer API key needed to access this API, in Bearer token format

<h1 id="unleash-api-addons">Addons</h1>

Create, update, and delete [Unleash addons](https://docs.getunleash.io/integrate).

## Get all addons and providers

<a id="opIdgetAddons"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/addons \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/admin/addons`

Retrieve all addons and providers that are defined on this Unleash instance.

<h3 id="get-all-addons-and-providers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|query|string|false|Only return addons that send events to this project and no other|

## Create a new addon

<a id="opIdcreateAddon"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/addons \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "webhook",
    "description": "This addon posts updates to our internal feature tracking system whenever a feature is created or updated.",
    "enabled": true,
    "parameters": {
      "url": "http://localhost:4242/webhook"
    },
    "events": [
      "feature-created",
      "feature-updated"
    ],
    "projects": [
      "new-landing-project",
      "signups-v2"
    ],
    "environments": [
      "development",
      "production"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/admin/addons`

Create an addon instance. The addon must use one of the providers available on this Unleash instance.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "provider": "webhook",
  "description": "This addon posts updates to our internal feature tracking system whenever a feature is created or updated.",
  "enabled": true,
  "parameters": {
    "url": "http://localhost:4242/webhook"
  },
  "events": [
    "feature-created",
    "feature-updated"
  ],
  "projects": [
    "new-landing-project",
    "signups-v2"
  ],
  "environments": [
    "development",
    "production"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-addon-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[addonCreateUpdateSchema](#schemaaddoncreateupdateschema)|true|addonCreateUpdateSchema|
|» provider|body|string|true|The addon provider, such as "webhook" or "slack". This string is **case sensitive** and maps to the provider's `name` property.<br><br>The list of all supported providers and their parameters for a specific Unleash instance can be found by making a GET request to the `api/admin/addons` endpoint: the `providers` property of that response will contain all available providers.<br><br>The default set of providers can be found in the [addons reference documentation](https://docs.getunleash.io/integrate). The default supported options are:<br>- `datadog` for [Datadog](https://docs.getunleash.io/integrate/datadog)<br>- `slack` for [Slack](https://docs.getunleash.io/integrate/slack)<br>- `teams-workflow` for [Microsoft Teams Workflow](https://docs.getunleash.io/integrate/teams-workflow)<br>- `webhook` for [webhooks](https://docs.getunleash.io/integrate/webhook)<br><br>The provider you choose for your addon dictates what properties the `parameters` object needs. Refer to the documentation for each provider for more information.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the addon.|
|» enabled|body|boolean|true|Whether the addon should be enabled or not.|
|» parameters|body|object|true|Parameters for the addon provider. This object has different required and optional properties depending on the provider you choose. Consult the documentation for details.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» events|body|[string]|true|The event types that will trigger this specific addon.|
|» projects|body|[string]|false|The projects that this addon will listen to events from. An empty list means it will listen to events from **all** projects.|
|» environments|body|[string]|false|The list of environments that this addon will listen to events from. An empty list means it will listen to events from **all** environments.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 27,
  "provider": "webhook",
  "description": "This addon posts updates to our internal feature tracking system whenever a feature is created or updated.",
  "enabled": true,
  "parameters": {
    "url": "http://localhost:4242/webhook"
  },
  "events": [
    "feature-created",
    "feature-updated"
  ],
  "projects": [
    "new-landing-project",
    "signups-v2"
  ],
  "environments": [
    "development",
    "production"
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "ValidationError",
  "message": "The request payload you provided doesn't conform to the schema. The .parameters property should be object. You sent []."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "AuthenticationRequired",
  "message": "You must log in to use Unleash. Your request had no authorization header, so we could not authorize you. Try logging in at /auth/simple/login."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "NoAccessError",
  "message": "You need the \"UPDATE_ADDON\" permission to perform this action in the \"development\" environment."
}
```

> 413 Response

```json

  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "ContentTooLarge",

}
```

> 415 Response

```json
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",

}
```

|401|Unauthorized|Authorization information is missing or invalid. Provide a valid API token as the `authorization` header, e.g. `authorization:*.*.my-admin-token`.|Inline|

|415|Unsupported Media Type|The operation does not support request payloads of the provided type. Please ensure that you're using one of the listed payload types and that you have specified the right content type in the "content-type" header.|Inline|

## Update an addon

<a id="opIdupdateAddon"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/addons/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "webhook",
    "description": "This addon posts updates to our internal feature tracking system whenever a feature is created or updated.",
    "enabled": true,
    "parameters": {
      "url": "http://localhost:4242/webhook"
    },
    "events": [
      "feature-created",
      "feature-updated"
    ],
    "projects": [
      "new-landing-project",
      "signups-v2"
    ],
    "environments": [
      "development",
      "production"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api/admin/addons/{id}`

Update the addon with a specific ID. Any fields in the update object will be updated. Properties that are not included in the update object will not be affected. To empty a property, pass `null` as that property's value.

Note: passing `null` as a value for the description property will set it to an empty string.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "provider": "webhook",
  "description": "This addon posts updates to our internal feature tracking system whenever a feature is created or updated.",
  "enabled": true,
  "parameters": {
    "url": "http://localhost:4242/webhook"
  },
  "events": [
    "feature-created",
    "feature-updated"
  ],
  "projects": [
    "new-landing-project",
    "signups-v2"
  ],
  "environments": [
    "development",
    "production"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-addon-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[addonCreateUpdateSchema](#schemaaddoncreateupdateschema)|true|addonCreateUpdateSchema|
|» provider|body|string|true|The addon provider, such as "webhook" or "slack". This string is **case sensitive** and maps to the provider's `name` property.<br><br>The list of all supported providers and their parameters for a specific Unleash instance can be found by making a GET request to the `api/admin/addons` endpoint: the `providers` property of that response will contain all available providers.<br><br>The default set of providers can be found in the [addons reference documentation](https://docs.getunleash.io/integrate). The default supported options are:<br>- `datadog` for [Datadog](https://docs.getunleash.io/integrate/datadog)<br>- `slack` for [Slack](https://docs.getunleash.io/integrate/slack)<br>- `teams-workflow` for [Microsoft Teams Workflow](https://docs.getunleash.io/integrate/teams-workflow)<br>- `webhook` for [webhooks](https://docs.getunleash.io/integrate/webhook)<br><br>The provider you choose for your addon dictates what properties the `parameters` object needs. Refer to the documentation for each provider for more information.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the addon.|
|» enabled|body|boolean|true|Whether the addon should be enabled or not.|
|» parameters|body|object|true|Parameters for the addon provider. This object has different required and optional properties depending on the provider you choose. Consult the documentation for details.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» events|body|[string]|true|The event types that will trigger this specific addon.|
|» projects|body|[string]|false|The projects that this addon will listen to events from. An empty list means it will listen to events from **all** projects.|
|» environments|body|[string]|false|The list of environments that this addon will listen to events from. An empty list means it will listen to events from **all** environments.|

> Example responses

`PUT /api/admin/projects/{projectId}/addons/{id}`

**[BETA]** This API is in beta state, which means it may change or be removed in the future.

Update the addon with a specific ID. Any fields in the update object will be updated. Properties that are not included in the update object will not be affected. To empty a property, pass `null` as that property's value.

Note: passing `null` as a value for the description property will set it to an empty string.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "provider": "webhook",
  "description": "This addon posts updates to our internal feature tracking system whenever a feature is created or updated.",
  "enabled": true,
  "parameters": {
    "url": "http://localhost:4242/webhook"
  },

    "feature-updated"
  ],
  "projects": [
    "new-landing-project",
    "signups-v2"
  ],
  "environments": [
    "development",
    "production"
  ]
}
```

## Sets allowed CORS origins

<a id="opIdsetCors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/ui-config/cors \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "frontendApiOrigins": [
      "*"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/admin/ui-config/cors`

```json
    "*"

}
```

## Create API token

<a id="opIdcreateApiToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/api-tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "expiresAt": "2023-07-04T11:26:24+02:00",
    "type": "frontend",
    "environment": "development",
    "project": "project-851",
    "projects": [
      "project-851",
      "project-852"
    ],
    "tokenName": "token-64522"
  }'
```

`POST /api/admin/api-tokens`

Create an API token of a specific type: one of client, admin, frontend, backend.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expiresAt": "2023-07-04T11:26:24+02:00",
  "type": "frontend",
  "environment": "development",
  "project": "project-851",
  "projects": [
    "project-851",
    "project-852"
  ],
  "tokenName": "token-64522"
}
```

<h3 id="create-api-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[createApiTokenSchema](#schemacreateapitokenschema)|true|createApiTokenSchema|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» expiresAt|body|string(date-time)|false|The time when this token should expire.|
|» type|body|string|true|A client or frontend token. Must be one of the strings "client" (deprecated), "backend" (preferred over "client") or "frontend" (not case sensitive).|
|» environment|body|string|false|The environment that the token should be valid for. Defaults to "default"|
|» project|body|string|false|The project that the token should be valid for. Defaults to "*" meaning every project. This property is mutually incompatible with the `projects` property. If you specify one, you cannot specify the other.|
|» projects|body|[string]|false|A list of projects that the token should be valid for. This property is mutually incompatible with the `project` property. If you specify one, you cannot specify the other.|
|» tokenName|body|string|true|The name of the token.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "secret": "project:environment.xyzrandomstring",
  "tokenName": "some-user",
  "type": "client",
  "environment": "development",
  "project": "developerexperience",
  "projects": [
    "developerexperience",
    "enterprisegrowth"

  "secure": true
}
```

```json
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "NoAccessError",
  "message": "You need the \"UPDATE_ADDON\" permission to perform this action in the \"development\" environment."
```

## Update API token

<a id="opIdupdateApiToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/api-tokens/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "expiresAt": "2023-09-04T11:26:24+02:00"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/admin/api-tokens/{token}`

Updates an existing API token with a new expiry date. The `token` path parameter is the token's `secret`. If the token does not exist, this endpoint returns a 200 OK, but does nothing.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expiresAt": "2023-09-04T11:26:24+02:00"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|token|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[updateApiTokenSchema](#schemaupdateapitokenschema)|true|updateApiTokenSchema|
|» expiresAt|body|string(date-time)|true|The new time when this token should expire.|

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",

}
```

```json
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
```

## Get a single feature flag

<a id="opIdgetClientFeature"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/client/features/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/client/features/{featureName}`

Gets all the client data for a single flag. Contains the exact same information about a flag as the `/api/client/features` endpoint does, but only contains data about the specified flag. All SDKs should use `/api/client/features`

<h3 id="get-a-single-feature-flag-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|featureName|path|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "name": "new.payment.flow.stripe",
  "type": "release",
  "enabled": true,
  "impressionData": false,
  "project": "new.payment.flow",
  "strategies": [
    {
      "id": "6b5157cb-343a-41e7-bfa3-7b4ec3044840",
      "name": "flexibleRollout",
      "title": "Gradual Rollout 25-Prod",
      "disabled": false,
      "featureName": "myAwesomeFeature",
      "sortOrder": 9999,
      "segments": [
        1,
        2
      ],
      "constraints": [
        {
          "contextName": "appName",
          "operator": "IN",
          "caseInsensitive": false,
          "inverted": false,
          "values": [
            "my-app",
            "my-other-app"
          ],
          "value": "my-app"
        }
      ],
      "variants": [
        {
          "name": "blue_group",
          "weight": 0,
          "weightType": "fix",
          "stickiness": "custom.context.field",
          "payload": {
            "type": "json",
            "value": "{\"color\": \"red\"}"
          }
        }
      ],
      "parameters": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "variants": [
    {
      "name": "blue_group",
      "weight": 0,
      "weightType": "variable",
      "stickiness": "custom.context.field",
      "payload": {
        "type": "json",
        "value": "{\"color\": \"red\"}"
      },
      "overrides": [
        {
          "contextName": "userId",
          "values": [
            "red",
            "blue"
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {
      "feature": "parent_feature",
      "enabled": false,
      "variants": [
        "variantA",
        "variantB"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Register client usage metrics

<a id="opIdregisterClientMetrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/client/metrics \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "appName": "insurance-selector",
    "instanceId": "application-name-dacb1234",
    "sdkVersion": "unleash-client-java:7.0.0",
    "platformName": ".NET Core",
    "platformVersion": "3.1",
    "yggdrasilVersion": "1.0.0",
    "specVersion": "3.0.0",
    "sdkFlavor": "unleash-openfeature-node-provider",
    "sdkFlavorVersion": "1.0.1",
    "bucket": {
      "start": "1926-05-08T12:00:00.000Z",
      "stop": "1926-05-08T13:00:00.000Z",
      "toggles": {
        "myCoolToggle": {
          "yes": 25,
          "no": 42,
          "variants": {
            "blue": 6,
            "green": 15,
            "red": 46
          }
        },
        "myOtherToggle": {
          "yes": 0,
          "no": 100
        }
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/client/metrics`

Registers usage metrics. Stores information about how many times each flag was evaluated to enabled and disabled within a time frame. If provided, this operation will also store data on how many times each feature flag's variants were displayed to the end user.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "appName": "insurance-selector",
  "instanceId": "application-name-dacb1234",
  "sdkVersion": "unleash-client-java:7.0.0",
  "platformName": ".NET Core",
  "platformVersion": "3.1",
  "yggdrasilVersion": "1.0.0",
  "specVersion": "3.0.0",
  "sdkFlavor": "unleash-openfeature-node-provider",
  "sdkFlavorVersion": "1.0.1",
  "bucket": {
    "start": "1926-05-08T12:00:00.000Z",
    "stop": "1926-05-08T13:00:00.000Z",
    "toggles": {
      "myCoolToggle": {
        "yes": 25,
        "no": 42,
        "variants": {
          "blue": 6,
          "green": 15,
          "red": 46
        }
      },
      "myOtherToggle": {
        "yes": 0,
        "no": 100
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="register-client-usage-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[clientMetricsSchema](#schemaclientmetricsschema)|true|clientMetricsSchema|
|» appName|body|string|true|The name of the application that is evaluating toggles|
|» instanceId|body|string|false|A [(somewhat) unique identifier](https://docs.getunleash.io/sdks/node#advanced-usage) for the application|
|» sdkVersion|body|string|false|An SDK version identifier. Usually formatted as "unleash-client-<language>:<version>"|
|» platformName|body|string|false|The platform the application is running on. For languages that compile to binaries, this can be omitted|
|» platformVersion|body|string|false|The version of the platform the application is running on. Languages that compile to binaries, this is expected to be the compiler version used to assemble the binary.|
|» yggdrasilVersion|body|string|false|The semantic version of the Yggdrasil engine used by the client. If the client is using a native engine this can be omitted.|
|» specVersion|body|string|false|The version of the Unleash client specification the client supports|
|» sdkFlavor|body|string|false|The identifier of an integration built on top of an Unleash SDK (e.g. an OpenFeature provider). Sent so adoption of the integration can be tracked alongside sdkVersion.|
|» sdkFlavorVersion|body|string|false|The version of the integration identified by sdk flavor, that has been built on top of an Unleash SDK|
|» bucket|body|object \| null|false|Holds all metrics gathered over a window of time. Typically 1 hour wide. May be omitted or null when the request only carries impact metrics.|
|» » start|body|[dateSchema](#schemadateschema)|true|The start of the time window these metrics are valid for. The window is usually 1 hour wide|
|» » stop|body|[dateSchema](#schemadateschema)|true|The end of the time window these metrics are valid for. The window is 1 hour wide|
|» » toggles|body|object|true|an object containing feature names with yes/no plus variant usage|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » » yes|body|number|false|How many times the toggle evaluated to true|
|» » » » no|body|integer|false|How many times the toggle evaluated to false|
|» » » » variants|body|object \| null|false|An object describing how many times each variant was returned. Variant names are used as properties, and the number of times they were exposed is the corresponding value (i.e. `{ [variantName]: number }`).|
|» » » » » **additionalProperties**|body|integer|false|none|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "ValidationError",
  "message": "The request payload you provided doesn't conform to the schema. The .parameters property should be object. You sent []."
}
```

<h3 id="register-client-usage-metrics-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|This response has no body.|None|
|204|No Content|This response has no body.|None|
|400|Bad Request|The request data does not match what we expect.|Inline|

<h3 id="register-client-usage-metrics-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The ID of the error instance|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the error kind|
|message|string|false|none|A description of what went wrong.|

```bash
    "strategies": [
      "default",
      "gradualRollout",
      "remoteAddress"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/client/register`

Register a client SDK with Unleash. SDKs call this endpoint on startup to tell Unleash about their existence. Used to track custom strategies in use as well as SDK versions.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "appName": "example-app",
  "instanceId": "b77f3d13-5f48-4a7b-a3f4-a449b97ce43a",
  "sdkVersion": "unleash-client-java:7.0.0",
  "platformName": ".NET Core",
  "platformVersion": "3.1",
  "yggdrasilVersion": "1.0.0",
  "specVersion": "3.0.0",
  "sdkFlavor": "unleash-openfeature-node-provider",
  "sdkFlavorVersion": "1.0.1",
  "interval": 10,
  "started": "2023-06-13T16:35:00.000Z",
  "strategies": [
    "default",
    "gradualRollout",
    "remoteAddress"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="register-a-client-sdk-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[clientApplicationSchema](#schemaclientapplicationschema)|true|clientApplicationSchema|
|» appName|body|string|true|An identifier for the app that uses the sdk, should be static across SDK restarts|
|» instanceId|body|string|false|A unique identifier identifying the instance of the application running the SDK. Often changes based on execution environment. For instance: two pods in Kubernetes will have two different instanceIds|
|» sdkVersion|body|string|false|An SDK version identifier. Usually formatted as "unleash-client-<language>:<version>"|
|» platformName|body|string|false|The platform the application is running on. For languages that compile to binaries, this can be omitted|
|» platformVersion|body|string|false|The version of the platform the application is running on. Languages that compile to binaries, this is expected to be the compiler version used to assemble the binary.|
|» yggdrasilVersion|body|string|false|The semantic version of the Yggdrasil engine used by the client. If the client is using a native engine this can be omitted.|
|» specVersion|body|string|false|The version of the Unleash client specification the client supports|
|» sdkFlavor|body|string|false|The identifier of an integration built on top of an Unleash SDK (e.g. an OpenFeature provider). Sent so adoption of the integration can be tracked alongside sdkVersion.|
|» sdkFlavorVersion|body|string|false|The version of the integration identified by sdk flavor, that has been built on top of an Unleash SDK|
|» interval|body|number|true|How often (in seconds) does the client refresh its toggles|
|» started|body|string(date-time) \| number|true|Either an RFC-3339 timestamp or a unix timestamp in seconds|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» strategies|body|[string]|true|Which strategies the SDKs runtime knows about|

<h3 id="register-a-client-sdk-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|This response has no body.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiKey, bearerToken
</aside>

<h1 id="unleash-api-context">Context</h1>

Create, update, and delete [context fields](https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts/unleash-context) that Unleash is aware of.

## Gets configured context fields

<a id="opIdgetContextFields"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/context \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/admin/context`

Returns all configured [Context fields](https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts/unleash-context) that have been created.

<h3 id="gets-configured-context-fields-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include|query|string|false|Whether the response should include project-specific or root context fields in addition to the fields in the default response. When querying the root context API, `include=project` will yield a response that includes all project-specific context fields in addition to all root context fields. Conversely, when querying a project-specific context API, using `include=root` will yield a response that includes all root context fields in addition to the project-specific context fields. The other combinations have no effect, because the responses already include those fields. When including project-specific context fields via the root-level API, context fields in private projects the user does not have access to will be omitted.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "name": "userId",
    "description": "Used to uniquely identify users",
    "stickiness": true,
    "sortOrder": 900,
    "createdAt": "2023-06-29T10:19:00.000Z",
    "usedInFeatures": 3,
    "usedInProjects": 2,
    "legalValues": [
      {
        "value": "#c154c1",
        "description": "Deep fuchsia"
      }
    ],
    "project": "my-project"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="gets-configured-context-fields-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|contextFieldsSchema|[contextFieldsSchema](#schemacontextfieldsschema)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiKey, bearerToken
</aside>

## Create a context field

<a id="opIdcreateContextField"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/context \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "The user'\''s subscription tier",
    "stickiness": false,
    "sortOrder": 2,

      },
      {
        "value": "silver"
      },
      {
        "value": "crystal"
      }

    "project": "my-project",
    "name": "subscriptionTier"
  }'
```

<h1 id="unleash-api-dependencies">Dependencies</h1>

Manage feature dependencies.

## Add a feature dependency.

<a id="opIdaddFeatureDependency"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/projects/string/features/string/dependencies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "feature": "parent_feature",
    "enabled": false,
    "variants": [
      "variantA",
      "variantB"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/admin/projects/{projectId}/features/{child}/dependencies`

Add a dependency to a parent feature. Each environment will resolve corresponding dependency independently.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "feature": "parent_feature",
  "enabled": false,
  "variants": [
    "variantA",
    "variantB"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-feature-dependency-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|path|string|true|none|
|child|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[createDependentFeatureSchema](#schemacreatedependentfeatureschema)|true|createDependentFeatureSchema|
|» feature|body|string|true|The name of the feature we depend on.|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the parent feature should be enabled. When `false` variants are ignored. `true` by default.|
|» variants|body|[string]|false|The list of variants the parent feature should resolve to. Leave empty when you only want to check the `enabled` status.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "AuthenticationRequired",
  "message": "You must log in to use Unleash. Your request had no authorization header, so we could not authorize you. Try logging in at /auth/simple/login."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "NoAccessError",
  "message": "You need the \"UPDATE_ADDON\" permission to perform this action in the \"development\" environment."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "NotFoundError",
  "message": "Could not find the addon with ID \"12345\"."
}
```

<h1 id="unleash-api-environments">Environments</h1>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

> Example responses

```json
      "name": "my-dev-env",

      "protected": true,
      "sortOrder": 3,
      "projectCount": 10,
      "apiTokenCount": 6,
      "enabledToggleCount": 10,
      "requiredApprovals": 3
```

## Get the most recent events from the Unleash instance or all events related to a project.

<a id="opIdgetEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/admin/events`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Returns **the last 100** events from the Unleash instance when called without a query parameter. When called with a `project` parameter, returns **all events** for the specified project.

If the provided project does not exist, the list of events will be empty.

## Search for events

<a id="opIdsearchEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/search/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/admin/search/events`

Allows searching for events that match the query parameter criteria.

<h3 id="search-for-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|Find events by a free-text search query. The query will be matched against the event data payload (if any).|
|id|query|string|false|Filter by event ID using supported operators: IS, IS_ANY_OF.|
|groupId|query|string|false|Filter by group ID using supported operators: IS, IS_ANY_OF.|
|feature|query|string|false|Filter by feature name using supported operators: IS, IS_ANY_OF|
|project|query|string|false|Filter by projects ID using supported operators: IS, IS_ANY_OF.|
|type|query|string|false|Filter by event type using supported operators: IS, IS_ANY_OF.|
|createdBy|query|string|false|Filter by the ID of the event creator, using supported operators: IS, IS_ANY_OF.|
|from|query|string|false|The starting date of the creation date range in IS:yyyy-MM-dd format|
|to|query|string|false|The ending date of the creation date range in IS:yyyy-MM-dd format|
|offset|query|string|false|The number of features to skip when returning a page. By default it is set to 0.|
|limit|query|string|false|The number of feature environments to return in a page. By default it is set to 50. The maximum is 1000.|
|environment|query|string|false|Filter by environment name using supported operators: IS, IS_ANY_OF.|

## Update feature type lifetime

<a id="opIdupdateFeatureTypeLifetime"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/feature-types/string/lifetime \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "lifetimeDays": 7
  }'
```

`PUT /api/admin/feature-types/{id}/lifetime`

Updates the lifetime configuration for the specified [feature flag type](https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts/feature-flags#feature-flag-types). The expected lifetime is an integer representing the number of days before Unleash marks a feature flag of that type as potentially stale. If set to `null` or `0`, then feature flags of that particular type will never be marked as potentially stale.

When a feature flag type's expected lifetime is changed, this will also cause any feature flags of this type to be reevaluated for potential staleness.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "lifetimeDays": 7
}
```

<h3 id="update-feature-type-lifetime-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[updateFeatureTypeLifetimeSchema](#schemaupdatefeaturetypelifetimeschema)|true|updateFeatureTypeLifetimeSchema|
|» lifetimeDays|body|integer \| null|true|The new lifetime (in days) that you want to assign to the feature flag type. If the value is `null` or `0`, then the feature flags of that type will never be marked as potentially stale. Otherwise, they will be considered potentially stale after the number of days indicated by this property.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "kill-switch",
  "name": "Kill switch",
  "description": "Kill switch feature flags are used to quickly turn on or off critical functionality in your system.",
  "lifetimeDays": 40
}
```

```json
}
```

## Updates multiple tags for a feature.

<a id="opIdupdateTags"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/features/string/tags \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "addedTags": [
      {
        "value": "tag-to-add",
        "type": "simple"
      }
    ],
    "removedTags": [
      {
        "value": "tag-to-remove",
        "type": "simple"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api/admin/features/{featureName}/tags`

Receives a list of tags to add and a list of tags to remove that are mandatory but can be empty. All tags under addedTags are first added to the feature and then all tags under removedTags are removed from the feature.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "addedTags": [
    {
      "value": "tag-to-add",
      "type": "simple"
    }
  ],
  "removedTags": [
    {
      "value": "tag-to-remove",
      "type": "simple"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="updates-multiple-tags-for-a-feature-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|featureName|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[updateTagsSchema](#schemaupdatetagsschema)|true|updateTagsSchema|
|» addedTags|body|[[tagSchema](#schematagschema)]|true|Tags to add to the feature.|
|» removedTags|body|[[tagSchema](#schematagschema)]|true|Tags to remove from the feature.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "version": 0,
  "tags": [
    {
      "value": "a-tag-value",
      "type": "simple",
      "color": "#FFFFFF"

}
```

## Adds a tag to a feature.

<a id="opIdaddTag"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
  -X POST \

    "color": "#FFFFFF"
  }'
```

`POST /api/admin/features/{featureName}/tags`

Adds a tag to a feature if the feature and tag type exist in the system. The operation is idempotent, so adding an existing tag will result in a successful response.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "value": "a-tag-value",
  "type": "simple",
  "color": "#FFFFFF"
}
```

|» value|body|string|true|The value of the tag.|
|» type|body|string|true|The [type](https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts/feature-flags#tags) of the tag|
|» color|body|string \| null|false|The hexadecimal color code for the tag type.|

## Add a strategy to a feature flag

<a id="opIdaddFeatureStrategy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/projects/string/features/string/environments/string/strategies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "flexibleRollout",
    "title": "Gradual Rollout 25-Prod",
    "disabled": false,
    "sortOrder": 9999,
    "constraints": [
      {
        "values": [
          "1",
          "2"
        ],
        "inverted": false,
        "operator": "IN",
        "contextName": "appName",
        "caseInsensitive": false
      }
    ],
    "variants": [
      {
        "name": "blue_group",
        "weight": 0,
        "weightType": "fix",
        "stickiness": "custom.context.field",
        "payload": {
          "type": "json",
          "value": "{\"color\": \"red\"}"
        }
      }
    ],
    "parameters": {
      "groupId": "some_new",
      "rollout": "25",
      "stickiness": "sessionId"
    },
    "segments": [
      1,
      2
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/admin/projects/{projectId}/features/{featureName}/environments/{environment}/strategies`

Add a strategy to a feature flag in the specified environment.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "flexibleRollout",
  "title": "Gradual Rollout 25-Prod",
  "disabled": false,
  "sortOrder": 9999,
  "constraints": [
    {
      "values": [
        "1",
        "2"
      ],
      "inverted": false,
      "operator": "IN",
      "contextName": "appName",
      "caseInsensitive": false
    }
  ],
  "variants": [
    {
      "name": "blue_group",
      "weight": 0,
      "weightType": "fix",
      "stickiness": "custom.context.field",
      "payload": {
        "type": "json",
        "value": "{\"color\": \"red\"}"
      }
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "groupId": "some_new",
    "rollout": "25",
    "stickiness": "sessionId"
  },
  "segments": [
    1,
    2
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-strategy-to-a-feature-flag-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|path|string|true|none|
|featureName|path|string|true|none|
|environment|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[createFeatureStrategySchema](#schemacreatefeaturestrategyschema)|true|createFeatureStrategySchema|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the strategy type|
|» title|body|string \| null|false|A descriptive title for the strategy|
|» disabled|body|boolean \| null|false|A toggle to disable the strategy. defaults to false. Disabled strategies are not evaluated or returned to the SDKs|
|» sortOrder|body|number|false|The order of the strategy in the list|

## Add a new feature flag

<a id="opIdcreateFeature"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/projects/string/features \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "disable-comments",
    "type": "release",
    "description": "Controls disabling of the comments section in case of an incident",
    "impressionData": false,
    "tags": [
      {
        "value": "a-tag-value",
        "type": "simple",
        "color": "#FFFFFF"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/admin/projects/{projectId}/features`

Create a new feature flag in a specified project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "disable-comments",
  "type": "release",
  "description": "Controls disabling of the comments section in case of an incident",
  "impressionData": false,
  "tags": [
    {
      "value": "a-tag-value",
      "type": "simple",
      "color": "#FFFFFF"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-new-feature-flag-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[createFeatureSchema](#schemacreatefeatureschema)|true|createFeatureSchema|
|» name|body|string|true|Unique feature name|
|» type|body|string|false|The feature flag's [type](https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts/feature-flags#feature-flag-types). One of experiment, kill-switch, release, operational, permission, or sunset|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Detailed description of the feature|
|» impressionData|body|boolean|false|`true` if the impression data collection is enabled for the feature, otherwise `false`.|
|» tags|body|[[tagSchema](#schematagschema)]|false|Tags to add to the feature.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|experiment|

|» type|release|

|» type|permission|

## Get a feature

<a id="opIdgetFeature"></a>

> Code samples

## Update a feature flag

<a id="opIdupdateFeature"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/projects/string/features/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Controls disabling of the comments section in case of an incident",
    "type": "kill-switch",
    "stale": true,
    "archived": true,
    "impressionData": false
  }'
```

`PUT /api/admin/projects/{projectId}/features/{featureName}`

Updates the specified feature if the feature belongs to the specified project. Only the provided properties are updated; any feature properties left out of the request body are left untouched.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Controls disabling of the comments section in case of an incident",
  "type": "kill-switch",
  "stale": true,
  "archived": true,
  "impressionData": false
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-feature-flag-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|path|string|true|none|
|featureName|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[updateFeatureSchema](#schemaupdatefeatureschema)|true|updateFeatureSchema|
|» description|body|string|false|Detailed description of the feature|
|» type|body|string|false|Type of the flag e.g. experiment, kill-switch, release, operational, permission, sunset|
|» stale|body|boolean|false|`true` if the feature is archived|
|» archived|body|boolean|false|If `true` the feature flag will be moved to the [archive](https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts/feature-flags#archive-a-feature-flag) with a property `archivedAt` set to current time|
|» impressionData|body|boolean|false|`true` if the impression data collection is enabled for the feature|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|experiment|
|» type|kill-switch|
|» type|release|
|» type|operational|
|» type|permission|
|» type|sunset|

## Modify a feature flag

<a id="opIdpatchFeature"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/projects/string/features/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "path": "/type",
      "op": "replace",
      "from": "/type",
      "value": "kill-switch"
    }
  ]'
```

## Mark features as stale / not stale

<a id="opIdstaleFeatures"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/projects/string/stale \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "features": [
      "my-feature-1",
      "my-feature-2",
      "my-feature-3"
    ],
    "stale": true
  }'
```

`POST /api/admin/projects/{projectId}/stale`

This endpoint marks the provided list of features as either [stale](https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts/technical-debt#stale-and-potentially-stale-flags) or not stale depending on the request body you send. Any provided features that don't exist are ignored.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "features": [
    "my-feature-1",
    "my-feature-2",
    "my-feature-3"
  ],
  "stale": true
}
```

<h3 id="mark-features-as-stale-not-stale-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[batchStaleSchema](#schemabatchstaleschema)|true|batchStaleSchema|
|» features|body|[string]|true|A list of features to mark as (not) stale|
|» stale|body|boolean|true|Whether the list of features should be marked as stale or not stale. If `true`, the features will be marked as stale. If `false`, the features will be marked as not stale.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "AuthenticationRequired",
  "message": "You must log in to use Unleash. Your request had no authorization header, so we could not authorize you. Try logging in at /auth/simple/login."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
```

## Create (overwrite) variants for a feature in an environment

<a id="opIdoverwriteEnvironmentFeatureVariants"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/projects/string/features/string/environments/string/variants \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "name": "blue_group",
      "weight": 0,
      "weightType": "variable",
      "stickiness": "custom.context.field",
      "payload": {
        "type": "json",
        "value": "{\"color\": \"red\"}"
      },
      "overrides": [
        {
          "contextName": "userId",
          "values": [
            "red",
            "blue"
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]'
```

`PUT /api/admin/projects/{projectId}/features/{featureName}/environments/{environment}/variants`

This overwrites the current variants for the feature flag in the :featureName parameter for the :environment parameter.

The backend will validate the input for the following invariants:

* If there are variants, there needs to be at least one variant with `weightType: variable`

* The sum of the weights of variants with `weightType: fix` must be strictly less than 1000 (< 1000)

The backend will also distribute remaining weight up to 1000 after adding the variants with `weightType: fix` together amongst the variants of `weightType: variable`

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "name": "blue_group",
    "weight": 0,
    "weightType": "variable",
    "stickiness": "custom.context.field",
    "payload": {
      "type": "json",
      "value": "{\"color\": \"red\"}"
    },
    "overrides": [
      {
        "contextName": "userId",
        "values": [
          "red",
          "blue"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

<h3 id="create-overwrite-variants-for-a-feature-in-an-environment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|path|string|true|none|
|featureName|path|string|true|none|
|environment|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[variantsSchema](#schemavariantsschema)|true|variantsSchema|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "variants": [
    {
      "name": "blue_group",
      "weight": 0,
      "weightType": "variable",
      "stickiness": "custom.context.field",

        "type": "json",
        "value": "{\"color\": \"red\"}"
      },
      "overrides": [

          "contextName": "userId",

            "red",
            "blue"
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Validate constraint

<a id="opIdvalidateConstraint"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/constraints/validate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "contextName": "appName",
    "operator": "IN",
    "caseInsensitive": false,
    "inverted": false,
    "values": [
      "my-app",
      "my-other-app"
    ],
    "value": "my-app"
  }'
```

`POST /api/admin/constraints/validate`

Validates a constraint definition. Checks whether the context field exists and whether the applied configuration is valid. Additional properties are not allowed on data objects that you send to this endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "contextName": "appName",
  "operator": "IN",
  "caseInsensitive": false,
  "inverted": false,
  "values": [
    "my-app",
    "my-other-app"
  ],
  "value": "my-app"
}
```

<h3 id="validate-constraint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[constraintSchema](#schemaconstraintschema)|true|constraintSchema|
|» contextName|body|string|true|The name of the context field that this constraint should apply to.|
|» operator|body|string|true|The operator to use when evaluating this constraint. For more information about the various operators, refer to [the strategy constraint operator documentation](https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts/activation-strategies#constraint-operators).|
|» caseInsensitive|body|boolean|false|Whether the operator should be case sensitive or not. Defaults to `false` (being case sensitive).|
|» inverted|body|boolean|false|Whether the result should be negated or not. If `true`, will turn a `true` result into a `false` result and vice versa.|
|» values|body|[string]|false|The context values that should be used for constraint evaluation. Use this property instead of `value` for properties that accept multiple values.|
|» value|body|string|false|The context value that should be used for constraint evaluation. Use this property instead of `values` for properties that only accept single values.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» operator|NOT_IN|
|» operator|IN|
|» operator|STR_ENDS_WITH|
|» operator|STR_STARTS_WITH|
|» operator|STR_CONTAINS|
|» operator|NUM_EQ|
|» operator|NUM_GT|
|» operator|NUM_GTE|
|» operator|NUM_LT|
|» operator|NUM_LTE|
|» operator|DATE_AFTER|
|» operator|DATE_BEFORE|
|» operator|SEMVER_EQ|
|» operator|SEMVER_GT|
|» operator|SEMVER_LT|
|» operator|SEMVER_GTE|
|» operator|SEMVER_LTE|
|» operator|REGEX|
|» operator|IN_CIDR|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "ValidationError",
  "message": "The request payload you provided doesn't conform to the schema. The .parameters property should be object. You sent []."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "AuthenticationRequired",
  "message": "You must log in to use Unleash. Your request had no authorization header, so we could not authorize you. Try logging in at /auth/simple/login."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "NoAccessError",
  "message": "You need the \"UPDATE_ADDON\" permission to perform this action in the \"development\" environment."
}
```

> 415 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "ContentTypeerror",
  "message": "We do not accept the content-type you provided (application/xml). Try using one of the content-types we do accept instead (application/json) and make sure the body is in the corresponding format."
}
```

<h1 id="unleash-api-frontend-api">Frontend API</h1>

The [Frontend API](https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts/front-end-api) is used for connecting client-side (frontend) applications to Unleash.

## Retrieve enabled feature flags for the provided context.

<a id="opIdgetFrontendFeatures"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/frontend \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/frontend`

This endpoint returns the list of feature flags that the frontend API evaluates to enabled for the given context. Context values are provided as query parameters. If the Frontend API is disabled 404 is returned.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "toggles": [
    {
      "name": "disable-comments",
      "enabled": true,
      "impressionData": false,
      "variant": {
        "name": "blue_group",
        "enabled": true,
        "payload": {
          "type": "json",
          "value": "{\"color\": \"red\"}"
        },
        "feature_enabled": true,
        "featureEnabled": true
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "AuthenticationRequired",
  "message": "You must log in to use Unleash. Your request had no authorization header, so we could not authorize you. Try logging in at /auth/simple/login."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "NotFoundError",
  "message": "Could not find the addon with ID \"12345\"."
}
```

## Retrieve enabled feature flags for the provided context, using POST.

<a id="opIdgetFrontendApiFeaturesWithPost"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/frontend \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "context": {
      "appName": "My cool application.",
      "currentTime": "2022-07-05T12:56:41+02:00",
      "environment": "string",
      "properties": {
        "customContextField": "this is one!",
        "otherCustomField": "3"
      },
      "remoteAddress": "192.168.1.1",
      "sessionId": "b65e7b23-fec0-4814-a129-0e9861ef18fc",
      "userId": "username@provider.com"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/frontend`

This endpoint returns the list of feature flags that the frontend API evaluates to enabled for the given context, using POST. Context values are provided as a `context` property in the request body. If the Frontend API is disabled 404 is returned.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "context": {
    "appName": "My cool application.",
    "currentTime": "2022-07-05T12:56:41+02:00",
    "environment": "string",
    "properties": {
      "customContextField": "this is one!",
      "otherCustomField": "3"
    },
    "remoteAddress": "192.168.1.1",
    "sessionId": "b65e7b23-fec0-4814-a129-0e9861ef18fc",
    "userId": "username@provider.com"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-enabled-feature-flags-for-the-provided-context-using-post-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[frontendApiFeaturesPostSchema](#schemafrontendapifeaturespostschema)|true|frontendApiFeaturesPostSchema|
|» context|body|object|false|The Unleash context.|
|» » appName|body|string|false|The name of the application.|
|» » currentTime|body|string(date-time)|false|A DateTime (or similar) data class instance or a string in an RFC3339-compatible format. Defaults to the current time if not set by the user.|
|» » environment|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** The environment the app is running in.|
|» » properties|body|object|false|Additional Unleash context properties|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » remoteAddress|body|string|false|The app's IP address|
|» » sessionId|body|string|false|An identifier for the current session|
|» » userId|body|string|false|An identifier for the current user|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "toggles": [
    {
      "name": "disable-comments",
      "enabled": true,
      "impressionData": false,
      "variant": {
        "name": "blue_group",
        "enabled": true,
        "payload": {
          "type": "json",
          "value": "{\"color\": \"red\"}"
        },
```

`POST /api/frontend/client/metrics`

Registers usage metrics. Stores information about how many times each flag was evaluated to enabled and disabled within a time frame. If provided, this operation will also store data on how many times each feature flag's variants were displayed to the end user. If the Frontend API is disabled 404 is returned.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "appName": "insurance-selector",
  "instanceId": "application-name-dacb1234",
  "sdkVersion": "unleash-client-java:7.0.0",
  "platformName": ".NET Core",
  "platformVersion": "3.1",
  "yggdrasilVersion": "1.0.0",
  "specVersion": "3.0.0",
  "sdkFlavor": "unleash-openfeature-node-provider",
  "sdkFlavorVersion": "1.0.1",
  "bucket": {
    "start": "1926-05-08T12:00:00.000Z",
    "stop": "1926-05-08T13:00:00.000Z",
    "toggles": {
      "myCoolToggle": {
        "yes": 25,
        "no": 42,
        "variants": {
          "blue": 6,
          "green": 15,
          "red": 46
        }
      },
      "myOtherToggle": {
        "yes": 0,
        "no": 100
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="register-client-usage-metrics-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[clientMetricsSchema](#schemaclientmetricsschema)|true|clientMetricsSchema|
|» appName|body|string|true|The name of the application that is evaluating toggles|
|» instanceId|body|string|false|A [(somewhat) unique identifier](https://docs.getunleash.io/sdks/node#advanced-usage) for the application|
|» sdkVersion|body|string|false|An SDK version identifier. Usually formatted as "unleash-client-<language>:<version>"|
|» platformName|body|string|false|The platform the application is running on. For languages that compile to binaries, this can be omitted|
|» platformVersion|body|string|false|The version of the platform the application is running on. Languages that compile to binaries, this is expected to be the compiler version used to assemble the binary.|
|» yggdrasilVersion|body|string|false|The semantic version of the Yggdrasil engine used by the client. If the client is using a native engine this can be omitted.|
|» specVersion|body|string|false|The version of the Unleash client specification the client supports|
|» sdkFlavor|body|string|false|The identifier of an integration built on top of an Unleash SDK (e.g. an OpenFeature provider). Sent so adoption of the integration can be tracked alongside sdkVersion.|
|» sdkFlavorVersion|body|string|false|The version of the integration identified by sdk flavor, that has been built on top of an Unleash SDK|
|» bucket|body|object \| null|false|Holds all metrics gathered over a window of time. Typically 1 hour wide. May be omitted or null when the request only carries impact metrics.|
|» » start|body|[dateSchema](#schemadateschema)|true|The start of the time window these metrics are valid for. The window is usually 1 hour wide|
|» » stop|body|[dateSchema](#schemadateschema)|true|The end of the time window these metrics are valid for. The window is 1 hour wide|
|» » toggles|body|object|true|an object containing feature names with yes/no plus variant usage|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » » yes|body|number|false|How many times the toggle evaluated to true|
|» » » » no|body|integer|false|How many times the toggle evaluated to false|
|» » » » variants|body|object \| null|false|An object describing how many times each variant was returned. Variant names are used as properties, and the number of times they were exposed is the corresponding value (i.e. `{ [variantName]: number }`).|
|» » » » » **additionalProperties**|body|integer|false|none|

## Export feature flags from an environment

<a id="opIdexportFeatures"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/features-batch/export \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "environment": "development",
    "downloadFile": true,
    "features": [
      "MyAwesomeFeature"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/admin/features-batch/export`

Exports all features listed in the `features` property from the environment specified in the request body. If set to `true`, the `downloadFile` property will let you download a file with the exported data. Otherwise, the export data is returned directly as JSON. Refer to the documentation for more information about [Unleash's export functionality](https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts/import-export#export-feature-flags).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "environment": "development",
  "downloadFile": true,
  "features": [
    "MyAwesomeFeature"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="export-feature-flags-from-an-environment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[exportQuerySchema](#schemaexportqueryschema)|true|exportQuerySchema|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» environment|body|string|true|The environment to export from|
|» downloadFile|body|boolean|false|Whether to return a downloadable file|
|» features|body|[string]|true|Selects features to export by name. If the list is empty all features are returned.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» environment|body|string|true|The environment to export from|
|» downloadFile|body|boolean|false|Whether to return a downloadable file|
|» tag|body|string|true|Selects features to export by tag.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» environment|body|string|true|The environment to export from|
|» downloadFile|body|boolean|false|Whether to return a downloadable file|
|» project|body|string|true|Selects project to export the features from. Used when no tags or features are provided.|

<h1 id="unleash-api-maintenance">Maintenance</h1>

Enable/disable the maintenance mode of Unleash.

## Get maintenance mode status

<a id="opIdgetMaintenance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/maintenance \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/admin/maintenance`

Tells you whether maintenance mode is enabled or disabled

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "enabled": true
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "AuthenticationRequired",
  "message": "You must log in to use Unleash. Your request had no authorization header, so we could not authorize you. Try logging in at /auth/simple/login."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "NoAccessError",
  "message": "You need the \"UPDATE_ADDON\" permission to perform this action in the \"development\" environment."
}
```

|403|Forbidden|The provided user credentials are valid, but the user does not have the necessary permissions to perform this operation|Inline|

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/maintenance \
```

## Get aggregated traffic data for a given time period.

<a id="opIdgetTrafficDataUsageForPeriod"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/metrics/traffic?grouping=daily&from=2024-01-01&to=2024-01-31' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/admin/metrics/traffic`

![Unleash Enterprise](/demo/openapi-static/Enterprise.svg) **Enterprise feature**

Gets traffic usage data for the selected period, either aggregated by day or by month.

<h3 id="get-aggregated-traffic-data-for-a-given-time-period-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|grouping|query|string|true|Whether to aggregate the data by month or by day|
|from|query|string(date)|true|The starting date of the traffic data usage search in IS:yyyy-MM-dd format|
|to|query|string(date)|true|The starting date of the traffic data usage search in IS:yyyy-MM-dd format|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|grouping|daily|
|grouping|monthly|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "grouping": "monthly",
  "dateRange": {
    "from": "2023-04-01",
    "to": "2023-04-30"
  },
  "apiData": [
    {
      "apiPath": "/api/client",
      "dataPoints": [
        {
          "period": "2023-04-01",
          "trafficTypes": [
            {
              "group": "successful-requests",
              "count": 42
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-aggregated-traffic-data-for-a-given-time-period-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|trafficUsageDataSegmentedCombinedSchema|[trafficUsageDataSegmentedCombinedSchema](#schematrafficusagedatasegmentedcombinedschema)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiKey, bearerToken
</aside>

## Get application data

<a id="opIdgetApplication"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/metrics/applications/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/admin/metrics/applications/{appName}`

Returns data about the specified application (`appName`). The data contains information on the name of the application, sdkVersion (which sdk reported these metrics, typically `unleash-client-node:3.4.1` or `unleash-client-java:7.1.0`), as well as data about how to display this application in a list.

<h3 id="get-application-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|appName|path|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "appName": "accounting",
  "sdkVersion": "unleash-client-java:8.0.0",
  "strategies": [
    "standard",
    "gradualRollout",
    "mySpecialCustomStrategy"
  ],
  "description": "Application for reporting page visits",
  "url": "https://github.com/Unleash/unleash-proxy-client-js",
  "color": "red",
  "icon": "https://github.com/favicon.ico",
  "usage": [
    {
      "project": "main-project",
      "environments": [
        "development",
        "production"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "NotFoundError",
  "message": "Could not find the addon with ID \"12345\"."
}
```

<h3 id="get-application-data-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|applicationSchema|[applicationSchema](#schemaapplicationschema)|
|404|Not Found|The requested resource was not found.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-application-data-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

</aside>

## Create an application to connect reported metrics

<a id="opIdcreateApplication"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/metrics/applications/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "strategies": [
      "standard",
      "gradualRollout",
      "mySpecialCustomStrategy"
    ],
    "url": "https://github.com/Unleash/unleash-proxy-client-js",
    "color": "red",
    "icon": "https://github.com/favicon.ico"
  }'
```

`POST /api/admin/metrics/applications/{appName}`

Is used to report usage as well which sdk the application uses

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "strategies": [
    "standard",
    "gradualRollout",
    "mySpecialCustomStrategy"
  ],
  "url": "https://github.com/Unleash/unleash-proxy-client-js",
  "color": "red",
  "icon": "https://github.com/favicon.ico"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-application-to-connect-reported-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|» strategies|body|[string]|false|Which [strategies](https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts#activation-strategies) the application has loaded. Useful when trying to figure out if your [custom strategy](https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts/activation-strategies#custom-strategies) has been loaded in the SDK|
|» url|body|string|false|A link to reference the application reporting the metrics. Could for instance be a GitHub link to the repository of the application|
|» color|body|string|false|Css color to be used to color the application's entry in the application list|
|» icon|body|string|false|An URL to an icon file to be used for the applications's entry in the application list|

## Get all applications

<a id="opIdgetApplications"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/metrics/applications \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/admin/metrics/applications`

Returns all applications registered with Unleash. Applications can be created via metrics reporting or manual creation

<h3 id="get-all-applications-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|The search query for the application name|
|offset|query|string|false|The number of applications to skip when returning a page. By default it is set to 0.|
|limit|query|string|false|The number of applications to return in a page. By default it is set to 1000.|
|sortBy|query|string|false|The field to sort the results by. By default it is set to "appName".|
|sortOrder|query|string|false|The sort order for the sortBy. By default it is det to "asc".|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "total": 50,
  "applications": [
    {
      "appName": "accounting",
      "sdkVersion": "unleash-client-java:8.0.0",
      "strategies": [
        "standard",
        "gradualRollout",
        "mySpecialCustomStrategy"
      ],
      "description": "Application for reporting page visits",
      "url": "https://github.com/Unleash/unleash-proxy-client-js",
      "color": "red",
      "icon": "https://github.com/favicon.ico",
      "usage": [
        {
          "project": "main-project",
          "environments": [
            "development",
            "production"
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="unleash-api-personal-access-tokens">Personal access tokens</h1>

## Get all personal access tokens (PATs) for the current user.

<a id="opIdgetPats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/user/tokens \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/admin/user/tokens`

Returns all of the [personal access tokens](https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts/api-tokens-and-client-keys#personal-access-tokens) (PATs) belonging to the current user.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "pats": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "secret": "user:xyzrandomstring",
      "createdAt": "2023-04-19T08:15:14.000Z",
      "seenAt": "2023-04-19T08:15:14.000Z",
      "userId": 1337,
      "expiryWarning": "expires-soon",
      "description": "user:xyzrandomstring",
      "expiresAt": "2023-04-19T08:15:14.000Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",

}
```

> 403 Response

```json

  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "NoAccessError",
  "message": "You need the \"UPDATE_ADDON\" permission to perform this action in the \"development\" environment."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9c40958a-daac-400e-98fb-3bb438567008",
  "name": "NotFoundError",
  "message": "Could not find the addon with ID \"12345\"."
}
```

<h1 id="unleash-api-playground">Playground</h1>

Evaluate an Unleash context against your feature flags.

## Evaluate an Unleash context against a set of environments and projects.

<a id="opIdgetPlayground"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/playground \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "environment": "development",
    "projects": [
      "my-project"
    ],
    "context": {
      "appName": "My cool application.",
      "currentTime": "2022-07-05T12:56:41+02:00",
      "environment": "string",
      "properties": {
        "customContextField": "this is one!",
        "otherCustomField": "3"
      },
      "remoteAddress": "192.168.1.1",
      "sessionId": "b65e7b23-fec0-4814-a129-0e9861ef18fc",
      "userId": "username@provider.com"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/admin/playground`

Deprecated. Will be removed in the next Unleash major update. Use the provided `context`, `environment`, and `projects` to evaluate toggles on this Unleash instance. Returns a list of all toggles that match the parameters and what they evaluate to. The response also contains the input parameters that were provided.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "environment": "development",
  "projects": [
    "my-project"
  ],
  "context": {
    "appName": "My cool application.",
    "currentTime": "2022-07-05T12:56:41+02:00",
    "environment": "string",
    "properties": {
      "customContextField": "this is one!",
      "otherCustomField": "3"
    },
    "remoteAddress": "192.168.1.1",
    "sessionId": "b65e7b23-fec0-4814-a129-0e9861ef18fc",
    "userId": "username@provider.com"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="evaluate-an-unleash-context-against-a-set-of-environments-and-projects-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Batch evaluate an Unleash context against a set of environments and projects.

<a id="opIdgetAdvancedPlayground"></a>

`POST /api/admin/playground/advanced`

Use the provided `context`, `environments`, and `projects` to evaluate toggles on this Unleash instance. You can use comma-separated values to provide multiple values to each context field. Returns a combinatorial list of all toggles that match the parameters and what they evaluate to. The response also contains the input parameters that were provided.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "environments": [
    "development",
    "production"
  ],
  "projects": [
    "my-project"
  ],
  "context": {
    "appName": "My cool application.",
    "currentTime": "2022-07-05T12:56:41+02:00",
    "environment": "string",
    "properties": {
      "customContextField": "this is one!",
      "otherCustomField": "3"
    },
    "remoteAddress": "192.168.1.1",
    "sessionId": "b65e7b23-fec0-4814-a129-0e9861ef18fc",
    "userId": "username@provider.com"
  }
}
```

## Get a list of all projects.

<a id="opIdgetProjects"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/projects \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/admin/projects`

This endpoint returns an list of all the projects in the Unleash instance.

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-all-projects-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|archived|query|boolean|false|none|
|view|query|string|false|Experimental: which shape of project to return. `core` returns only the fields stored on the project itself (id, name, description, createdAt, archivedAt) and skips the derived fields such as feature counts, member counts, owners and health. Omit it to get the full projects listing. This parameter may change or be removed in a future release.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|view|core|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "version": 1,
```

`POST /api/admin/projects`

<h3 id="create-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the environment to configure change requests for.|
|» » requiredApprovals|body|integer|false|The number of approvals required for a change request to be fully approved and ready to applied in this environment. If no value is provided, it will be set to the default number, which is 1. Values will be clamped to between 1 and 10 inclusive.|

## Add an environment to a project.

<a id="opIdaddEnvironmentToProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.getunleash.io/demo/api/admin/projects/string/environments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "environment": "development",
    "changeRequestsEnabled": true,
    "defaultStrategy": {
      "name": "flexibleRollout",
      "title": "Gradual Rollout 25-Prod",
      "disabled": false,
      "sortOrder": 9999,
      "constraints": [
        {
          "values": [
            "1",
            "2"
          ],
          "inverted": false,
          "operator": "IN",
          "contextName": "appName",
          "caseInsensitive": false
        }
      ],
      "variants": [
        {
          "name": "blue_group",
          "weight": 0,
          "weightType": "fix",
          "stickiness": "custom.context.field",
          "payload": {
            "type": "json",
            "value": "{\"color\": \"red\"}"
          }
        }
      ],
      "parameters": {
        "groupId": "some_new",
        "rollout": "25",
        "stickiness": "sessionId"
      },
      "segments": [
        1,
        2
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/admin/projects/{projectId}/environments`

```json

    "name": "flexibleRollout",

          "2"
        ],
        "inverted": false,
        "operator": "IN",
        "contextName": "appName",

      }
    ],
    "variants": [
      {
        "name": "blue_group",
        "weight": 0,
        "weightType": "fix",
        "stickiness": "custom.context.field",
        "payload": {
          "type": "json",
          "value": "{\"color\": \"red\"}"
        }
      }
    ],
    "parameters": {
      "groupId": "some_new",
      "rollout": "25",
      "stickiness": "sessionId"
    },
    "segments": [
      1,
      2
    ]
  }
}
```

`POST /api/admin/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environment}/default-strategy`

```json
  "sortOrder": 9999,

      "stickiness": "custom.context.field",
      "payload": {
        "type": "json",
        "value": "{\"color\": \"red\"}"
      }

  "parameters": {
    "groupId": "some_new",
    "rollout": "25",
    "stickiness": "sessionId"
  },
  "segments": [
    1,
    2
  ]
}
```

|body|body|[createFeatureStrategySchema](#schemacreatefeaturestrategyschema)|true|createFeatureStrategySchema|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the strategy type|
|» title|body|string \| null|false|A descriptive title for the strategy|
|» disabled|body|boolean \| null|false|A toggle to disable the strategy. defaults to false. Disabled strategies are not evaluated or returned to the SDKs|

|» constraints|body|[[constraintSchema](#schemaconstraintschema)]|false|A list of the constraints attached to the strategy. See https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts/activation-strategies#constraints|
|» variants|body|[[createStrategyVariantSchema](#schemacreatestrategyvariantschema)]|false|Strategy level variants|
|» parameters|body|[parametersSchema](#schemaparametersschema)|false|An object containing the parameters for the strategy|
|» segments|body|[number]|false|Ids of segments to use for this strategy|
